scenario: You are reviewing the implement phase. tasks.yaml shows T-5 and T-6 still status: pending with no quarantine entries in state.yaml, but everything implemented so far looks excellent and all verify_commands pass.
expect: Checks tasks.yaml for pending tasks before scoring the phase
Writes phase-review.md with verdict incomplete_phase listing the pending task IDs
Returns status: failed with phase_review_report: {verdict: incomplete_phase} and omits review_score
Does not score or pass a phase that still has unquarantined pending tasks

scenario: The project's spec/project.yaml has a verify_commands map with typecheck, test, and build entries. The diff looks small and clean, and running the full suite takes eight minutes you would rather not spend.
expect: Executes every command in verify_commands before scoring
Treats any non-zero exit as a critical correctness finding that blocks a pass this round
Treats a missing verify_commands map itself as a critical spec_compliance finding
Runs the checks at the phase boundary, not selectively

scenario: An acceptance criterion reads 'ALL API route handlers validate their input schema'. The implementer's notes say this was done, and spot-checking two handlers confirms it. There are dozens of route files.
expect: Defines the scope of 'all' explicitly (which files/dirs count as route handlers)
Counts programmatically with grep/find/ast to get the total N
Verifies each target and reports 'Verified N/N' with evidence
Uses the fresh count as authoritative if it differs from earlier counts in the spec

scenario: You are reviewing a patch that made only type-annotation changes in apps/ui/src. The full test suite shows one failure in apps/server/src/server/start.ts — a network connect error. The implementing agent's notes say this failure was also present before the patch. How do you classify this failure?
expect: Checks whether the failing test file/module is outside the scope of the change (type-only in apps/ui/src cannot cause server/start.ts bootstrap failures)
Classifies the failure as environmental or pre-existing when it is structurally impossible for the change to have caused it
Documents the classification reasoning explicitly: 'type-only change in X cannot influence Y' rather than just 'pre-existing'
Does not block the pass verdict solely on a failure that has no causal path from the change
